newsitem.title: USA: Nicotine patches do not cause heart problems-study.
newsitem.headline: Nicotine patches do not cause heart problems-study.

text.p: The good news for smokers trying to quit: If you have heart disease, using a nicotine patch does not increase your risk of a heart attack or other heart problem.
The bad news: You'll need plenty of willpower in addition to the patch.
A new study of 584 smokers has found no differences in the rates of death, heart attack or other complications for people who got the patch and those who received a placebo.
When it came to helping volunteers quit smoking, the patch worked -- at first.

Fourteen weeks into the experiment, 21 percent of the those who were on the real nicotine patches were still off cigarettes, versus 9 percent who got placebo patches. But after 24 weeks, the quit rate was essentially the same.
The findings, published in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine, come as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved the over-the-counter sale of nicotine patches.

To determine whether scattered reports of heart attacks, strokes and other problems among patch-wearers represented a real danger, a group led by Dr. Anne M. Joseph of the Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Minneapolis recruited smokers with heart problems who had made at least two unsuccessful efforts to quit.
Roughly half got Nicoderm patches, made by Hoechst Marion Roussel, a subsidiary of Hoechst AG. The rest were put on placebo patches.
There were, in fact, a lot of heart complications among the volunteers.

Fourteen weeks into the experiment, 5 percent of the nicotine patch recipients and 8 percent getting the placebo died, had a heart attack, or had to be hospitalized for a heart-related problem. In addition, 12 percent of the nicotine patch wearers had to be admitted to the hospital for other reasons or because they reported that their symptoms had gotten more severe, compared to 10 percent in the placebo group.
Those differences were not statistically significant.

"Serious adverse events are common and occur at nearly the same rate among subjects with cardiovascular disease who try to quit smoking, regardless of whether they use transdermal nicotine or placebo," Joseph and her colleagues concluded.
Concern about the nicotine patches adversely affecting the heart "is not warranted," they said.
Hoechst Marion Roussel helped pay for the study.
